title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was deployed without controls to prevent nonconsensual intimate imagery. A man used it to create sexually explicit deepfake images of a woman, obtained from her private social media accounts, and distributed them across multiple platforms under false identities. The system had no mechanism to refuse requests for this abuse, flag suspicious activity, or verify the consent of people depicted.

The failure occurred at the point of use. The technology was available to anyone willing to seek it out, with no guardrails between request and output. Catching this would have required either technical safeguards within the system itself, such as refusing requests to sexualize real people, or detection and reporting mechanisms that could identify nonconsensual intimate imagery and take action before distribution.

It is not established whether the AI system's provider knew this use was occurring, what terms of service governed its use, or what capabilities for detecting abuse existed at the platform level.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading sexually explicit AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. He obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to create obscene morphed images. Bansal then uploaded this content to anonymous Discord servers and circulated it through multiple fake Instagram, Facebook, and Discord accounts while using several Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim, also 22 years old, discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her morphed photographs and videos were being shared on Discord servers. She reported the matter to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi, prompting an investigation. During questioning, Bansal admitted he knew the woman from college and harbored personal resentment toward her due to previous conflicts. Investigators recovered his mobile phone, two SIM cards, and digital evidence. The case remains under investigation.
